content.text: Kop (also known as Cop) is a traditional Polish trick-taking game that is a cultural staple of the Greater Poland (Wielkopolska) region. Played with a highly condensed 16-card deck, it is celebrated for its extreme speed and complex partnership dynamics. It is a descendant of the German Schafkopf and is the sister game to the Kashubian BaÅ›ka.

Developed from the German Schafkopf game in the 19th century, Kop was adapted by Polish players in regions under Prussian influence. It became a distinct Polish identity game through the inclusion of the 'Wedding' (Wesele) contract.
4 players playing in partnerships or solo depending on the contract.

items.text: As-dycha (classic): Classic order: 12 trumps (Hearts A-10, Q-J, Diamonds A-10), clubs and spades two cards each.
As-trzy dychy: Black tens promoted above club Queen; 14 trumps, one card each in clubs and spades.
Kontra to own wesele: Some allow a player to say kontra to their own wesele (not to zolo or zolo du).
